repairAudit.method: Tested against G22 v1's own fields rather than against my finding's prose. A repair composed from my wording would have failed the source-equality checks below.

repairAudit.statesNowCarryState: Four states where v1 had one, and they are genuinely distinguished: four distinct ids, four distinct platform values, four distinct stateNamed values. Each names a platform cell under the hostility family and carries the four live-cell members. This is what v1 lacked entirely.
repairAudit.platformsExactlyTheSource: The four platform values are macos/arm64, macos/x86_64, linux/x86_64, linux/arm64 — equal in order and content to G22 v1's own platforms key. No fifth platform, and Windows is absent, which matters because G22 v1 records Windows as deferred and not a cell.

overCorrectionAudit.whyThisWasTheRealRisk: On this gate the only route to naming states runs alongside forbidden material — the class's left axis is OS/filesystem/architecture, and two of its coordinates are reserved TCB selectors. A repair that named states by populating those selectors would have traded one defect for a prohibition breach. That was the thing to check.
overCorrectionAudit.reservedAxesUntouched: filesystemSelector and versionOrBuildSelector are the literal string RESERVED at top level and in all four states — eight occurrences, no value anywhere. Zero filesystem type names of any kind. Zero version or build literals: the only decimal in the artifact is the 7.1 of the section-recipe refusal, which I checked rather than assumed.
overCorrectionAudit.noTableContent: Zero ikconfig vectors — the two ikconfig mentions are in whatIsNotAuthored and doesNot as refusals. Zero fixture paths. No per-OS dependency table of any kind.
overCorrectionAudit.platformsAreNotReserved: Naming the four D-002 platforms is not populating a reserved table: G22 v1 publishes them in a top-level platforms key and in the class's own exactByteIntent, and its passProperty requires every D-002-platform cell to be present. The reserved axes are the filesystem selector and the version/build selector, both of which remain unpopulated.
overCorrectionAudit.hostilityFamilyNotDecomposed: All four stateNamed values end with the whole phrase 'hostile loader/system library/tool environment'. G22 v1's slashJoiner records that loader/system library/tool stays one hostility family, and the repair respects it rather than splitting the family into three sub-kinds it would have had to invent.
overCorrectionAudit.ntTcbIdentifiers: The artifact refuses NT-TCB-1, NT-TCB-2 and NT-TCB-3 by name, which raised the question whether enumerating three numbers coins them. It does not: all three already exist in the corpus, appearing in 69, 54 and 58 files respectively including the platform-tcb-contract lineage. Refusing real identifiers is not minting them.
overCorrectionAudit.rosetta: Not invented. The macos/x86_64 state carries a rosettaStanding that excludes it, and the other four mentions are refusals. See consideredAndDeclined on the wording.

consideredAndDeclined.candidate: Raising the rosettaStanding as a truncation of the source field of the same name
consideredAndDeclined.why: Declined, and recorded precisely so the coordinator can weigh it independently. G22 v1's rosettaStanding reads 'Never Rosetta. macos/x86_64 is native Intel-class hardware, never Rosetta-on-Apple-Silicon (D-006). A translated macos/x86_64 cell is not a pass.' The state carries the first two sentences and drops the D-006 attribution and the final pass clause. Four reasons not to grade it. The field is unmarked, and this corpus signals byte-equality with a Verbatim suffix which this key does not carry, so no equality is claimed. The substance — the exclusion of Rosetta — is preserved, and the dropped sentence restates its consequence rather than adding a condition. The source is pinned by digest one object away. And v1 carried no rosettaStanding at all, so this is a voluntary addition; grading a shortened voluntary refusal would discourage adding it. I record the exact dropped text rather than only my conclusion.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Nineteen attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject ac36a447 at 0444, 9356 bytes, unmoved at both ends; v1 unmoved at b5eb39e3 and not overwritten; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and the artifact's head equals it; live required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All nine cited pins reproduce, and the artifact's nine 64-hex strings are exactly those pins. The v1 SHOULD-FIX is landed with real content. Where v1 had one record holding only the class name, v2 has four genuinely distinguished states — four distinct ids, platforms and stateNamed values — each naming a platform cell under the hostility family, carrying the four live-cell members, citing the source clause, and marking both reserved selectors. The per-state record grew from four fields to ten. Crucially the material is carried rather than composed: the four platforms equal G22 v1's platforms key in order and content, the four members equal its liveCellMemberSplit.membersInOrder, and each state cites the class's exactByteIntent as its source. On this gate the over-correction risk was the real one and I want it on the record. The repair I specified required naming platforms, which sits one step from forbidden reserved-table content, so a successor could easily have traded the defect for a prohibition breach. It did not. filesystemSelector and versionOrBuildSelector are the literal string RESERVED in eight places with no value anywhere; there are zero filesystem type names, zero version or build literals — the only decimal in the file is the 7.1 of the section-recipe refusal, which I checked rather than assumed — and zero ikconfig vectors. Naming the four D-002 platforms is not table population: G22 v1 publishes them openly and its passProperty requires every one as a cell, while the reserved axes are the two selectors, untouched. The hostility family is also kept whole in all four stateNamed values rather than split into three sub-kinds that would have had to be invented, respecting G22 v1's slashJoiner. One thing looked like a new invention and was tested: the artifact refuses NT-TCB-1, NT-TCB-2 and NT-TCB-3 by name, which raised whether enumerating three numbers coins them. All three pre-exist across dozens of corpus files, so refusing them mints nothing. No predecessor role claims 'this v2', and the v1 verdict is described accurately and without softening. One thing declined and recorded in full: the macos/x86_64 state's rosettaStanding carries the first two sentences of G22 v1's field of the same name and drops the D-006 attribution and the clause 'A translated macos/x86_64 cell is not a pass.' I set out the exact dropped text and my four reasons for not grading it — the key is unmarked where this corpus signals byte-equality with a Verbatim suffix, the Rosetta exclusion itself is preserved, the source is pinned one object away, and v1 carried no rosettaStanding at all so this is a voluntary addition. Disclosure: this successor exists to land my own finding and pins my v1 verdict, the second time this session I have reviewed a repair of my own objection. I graded against G22 v1's fields rather than my prose, ran the over-correction pass this gate demands, and tested the NT-TCB identifiers against the corpus. Having specified the repair shape, I am poorly placed to notice a better repair not taken; a Codex pass would be worth more than usual.
